haiku-low.q1: If reports.row_count is 10,000 or fewer, the CSV is returned in the click's response. Above 10,000, or if the count is missing, a record is created and the job emails a link.
haiku-low.q2: The second click returns the user's existing active export of that report with 200, and nothing new starts. Its filters may be the old ones, which the page shows.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link works for 24 hours. The exports bucket lifecycle rule deletes the file 7 days after creation. The plan adds no cleanup job.
haiku-low.q4: At most 3 attempts. After the third failure, the export is marked failed, parts are aborted, an export_failed email is sent, and the page shows Try again.
haiku-low.q5: The read replica. Report rows are read only from it, never from the primary database.
haiku-low.q6: In the primary-database table report_exports. The page polls GET /exports/latest while active, so reopening the page shows the current state.
haiku-low.q7: It reads 10,000-row keyset batches, buffers whole CSV lines into 8 MB parts, uploads each as a multipart part, and checkpoints after each. It never holds the whole report.
haiku-low.q8: Uploaded parts stay invisible in the bucket, and the checkpoint records parts and last_row_id. The next attempt resumes from last_row_id; rows after the checkpoint are reread.
haiku-low.q9: They are normalised and stored on the report_exports record in the primary database. The job reads them from that record by export_id, not from the payload.
haiku-low.q10: A unique partial index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running. The conflicting second insert fails and the request returns the first export.
haiku-low.q11: The export must be done with email_sent_at empty. The job then makes a 24-hour signed URL, sends the email, and sets email_sent_at. A rerun after that does nothing.
haiku-low.q12: The whole CSV is built in memory before the 200 is sent, so a failure returns an error with Retry. The user gets no partial file, and nothing is stored.

sonnet.q1: The API reads reports.row_count (unfiltered total). If it is 10,000 or fewer, it takes the small path; if it is above 10,000 or missing, the large path. Small path: the click's own response is the CSV (200, text/csv, attachment report-{report_id}.csv), saved by the browser after the full response arrives. Large path: the response is the export record (202; the page then shows its state), and the user later gets an email with a 24-hour download link.
sonnet.q2: Nothing new starts. A unique partial index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running allows one active export. The insert hits the index, the API rolls back, reads the user's active export for this report and returns it with 200. Caveat: if the user changed filters, they get the earlier export with the old filters (open question 1).
sonnet.q3: The emailed link is a signed URL valid for 24 hours (86400 seconds). It is a bearer link, so anyone holding it can download it, even after the user loses report.view. No cleanup job removes the file: the exports bucket lifecycle rule deletes every object 7 days after it was created (at completion).
sonnet.q4: At most 3 attempts (waits of 60 s before attempt 2 and 300 s before attempt 3). After the third failure, on_final_failure runs. It aborts the multipart upload if there is one, sets the record to failed with error "export failed after 3 attempts" and completed_at, and sends an "export_failed" email. The page shows failed with the error message and a Try again button. Exception: if the status is already done (only the email failed), the status stays done, the link still shows on the page and email_sent_at stays empty for an operator to resend.
sonnet.q5: The read replica (report_rows is read only from it, never from the primary). The only exception is reports.row_count, which is metadata and may come from the primary or the replica.
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports table (export record) on the primary database, in the status column (queued, running, done, failed). The page calls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest on load, on click and on return, and polls every 3 to 5 seconds while the status is queued or running, stopping at done or failed. The page keeps no state of its own, so the state survives a reload or later return. For done it adds a fresh 24-hour signed URL, or returns expired if completed_at is over 7 days ago or the object is gone.
sonnet.q7: It streams. It reads batches of up to 10,000 rows from the replica using keyset paging, formats them as CSV lines into a buffer, and uploads each 8 MB as one multipart part. The memory held is one batch plus one buffer, about 30 MB, never the whole report. About 900 MB of CSV is about 115 parts, under the 10,000-part limit. Complete_multipart then makes the file visible atomically.
sonnet.q8: Parts already uploaded stay in the bucket as an incomplete, invisible multipart upload (discarded after 24 hours if never completed), and the checkpoint (parts, last_row_id, rows_written) stays on the export record. The next attempt reuses the upload and resumes from last_row_id, with an empty buffer. Rows after the checkpoint (the lost buffer) are read again. A part uploaded but not checkpointed is replaced by the same-numbered part. If the upload is gone, the upload fields are cleared and the next attempt starts fresh from the first row.
sonnet.q9: The browser sends filters and cols (read from the page URL) as JSON in the POST. The API validates and normalises them and stores them in the filters and cols columns of the report_exports record. The job gets only {"export_id": id} as its payload and reads filters and cols from the record.
sonnet.q10: The unique partial index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running, in the primary database. The second insert waits for the first commit, fails on the index, and the API returns the first export.
sonnet.q11: The export must be done, meaning complete_multipart succeeded and the fenced update set status done and completed_at. The record also needs email_sent_at empty, and report.view must still hold for the user (rechecked in step 6). It then makes a 24-hour signed URL, sends the email, and sets email_sent_at in a fenced update. On a rerun the job loads the record. If status is failed, or done with email_sent_at set, it ends and does nothing. If done with email_sent_at empty, it skips to the email step and sends it, so a crash between send and flag write can cause one duplicate.
sonnet.q12: The CSV is fully built in memory before any 200 status is sent. A replica error or the 60-second timeout returns an error status, the browser shows an error with a Retry button, and the user never gets a partial file. Nothing is stored.
